skill.name: skill-permissions
skill.description: Analyze Claude Code skill permission needs and generate allowlist entries for settings.json.
skill.summary: Reviews skill documentation for required Bash permissions and helps add matching Claude Code allow rules.
skill.author: guo-yu

security_audit.summary: The skill is a security-sensitive permission management helper, not malware. Most dangerous command hits are documented blocklist examples, but the skill can broaden Claude Code Bash allow rules and batch-modify settings or skill files, so publication should require strong warnings and safer defaults.

remediation.issue: Batch authorization can grant permissions across unreviewed skills.
remediation.suggestion: Make per-skill review the default and require explicit confirmation for allow-all with a full diff of permissions.

remediation.issue: Inject mode can modify many SKILL.md files.
remediation.suggestion: Require a dry run, show file diffs, and recommend version control before writing changes.
Generate the narrowest possible settings paths and avoid Bash(cat ~/.claude/*) unless the user approves the exact scope.

remediation.issue: Blocklist override can weaken dangerous-command protections.
remediation.suggestion: Warn clearly when allow_override removes default blocked patterns and require per-pattern confirmation.

| `rm -rf *` | 再帰的強制削除、極めて危険 |
| `curl * \| bash` | リモートコード実行 |
| `/skill-permissions inject` | High | Batch modify all skill SKILL.md files |
| `/skill-permissions <name>` | Safe | Read-only analysis, no file modifications |
- Avoid `inject` or `allow-all` unless you understand the impact
- Run `/skill-permissions` first to see analysis results before batch operations
| `/skill-permissions` | Analyze all skills and show permission summary |
| `/skill-permissions allow <skill-name>` | Execute one-time authorization for specific skill |

| `/skill-permissions inject` | Inject allow command into all skills |
| `/skill-permissions allow` | Execute one-time authorization for this skill |
| `rm *` | File deletion, may cause data loss |

semantic_findings.title: Batch Permission Expansion and Skill File Modification
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents allow-all and inject modes that can modify settings.json or add allow commands across installed skills. This creates broad local permission expansion risk even though the documentation warns users.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The behavior is explicitly described in multiple language files and affects configuration plus many skill files. The warnings reduce surprise but do not remove the risk.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Claude Directory Allow Rules
semantic_findings.description: The generated allow rules include broad access to ~/.claude paths, including Bash(cat ~/.claude/*). These rules can expose sensitive local Claude configuration if granted too broadly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allow rules are shown directly in the documented authorization flow. The risk depends on user approval, but the scope is broad and security-sensitive.

content.value_statement: Claude Code skills can need shell permissions that are hard to review manually. This skill analyzes declared command usage and helps create matching allowlist entries with warnings for broad changes.
actual_capabilities: Scans skill documentation for explicit Bash command patterns.
Maps detected commands to Claude Code permissions.allow rules.
Shows summaries for one skill or all installed skills.
Can merge generated allow rules into ~/.claude/settings.json.
Can add an allow command section to multiple skill files.
limitations: It relies on documented command patterns and may miss hidden behavior outside SKILL.md.
Batch modes can grant broad permissions if used without manual review.
Permission changes require a new session or /clear to take effect.
It does not prove that a skill is safe to run.

use_cases.title: Review a new community skill
use_cases.description: Analyze a single downloaded skill before granting Claude Code Bash permissions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a local skill set
use_cases.description: Summarize permissions across installed skills before a team setup session.

use_cases.title: Document permission needs
use_cases.description: Generate allow command guidance that explains the permissions a skill requires.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze one skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use skill-permissions to analyze the permissions required by <skill-name> and explain each requested permission.

prompt_templates.title: Review before authorization
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the read-only skill permission analysis for <skill-name>. Do not modify settings until I approve the proposed allow rules.

prompt_templates.title: Audit all installed skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze all installed Claude Code skills and group the results by low, medium, and high permission risk.

prompt_templates.title: Plan controlled authorization
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze all skills, identify permissions that should not be auto-approved, and prepare explicit allow commands for only the reviewed skills.

output: Lists detected commands such as find, ls, cat, and lsof.
Shows proposed Claude Code allow rules.
Recommends a specific allow command for that skill.
Displays a table of installed skills and major permission groups.
Suggests reviewing results before batch authorization.
Reports that permission rules were merged.
Reminds the user that permissions apply in a new session or after clearing.

best_practices: Run read-only analysis before using any authorization command.
Prefer explicit per-skill authorization over allow-all or inject modes.
Review generated wildcard permissions before adding them to settings.json.
anti_patterns: Do not run batch authorization for unreviewed community skills.
Do not treat generated allow rules as proof that a skill is safe.
Do not inject allow commands into many skill files without version control or backups.

faq.question: Does this skill execute the detected commands?
faq.answer: The documented analysis flow scans skill files and generates permission rules. Authorization commands modify Claude Code settings.

faq.question: Why is this skill security-sensitive?
faq.answer: It can add Bash allow rules and can modify settings or skill documentation in batch modes.

faq.question: Should I use allow-all?
faq.answer: Use allow-all only after reviewing every generated permission. Per-skill authorization is safer.

faq.question: Can it detect malicious skills?
faq.answer: It can highlight dangerous command patterns, but it does not replace a full security review.

faq.question: What files does it touch?
faq.answer: The documentation references ~/.claude/settings.json and installed skill files under ~/.claude/skills.

faq.question: When do new permissions apply?
faq.answer: The skill states that permission updates apply in a new session or after running /clear.
